aspect: Interpretation changes what can be said
description: Trauma disclosure through a third person, often from the same community, frequently stops the disclosure entirely - particularly for sexual violence, collaboration, and anything the community would judge.
energy_note: A translator from your own city, in the room.

description: Specialist trauma services in most destination countries run six to eighteen month waits. The person presents at the point of crisis and is offered an appointment after the crisis has resolved itself one way or another.
energy_note: Booked in for after it stops mattering.

aspect: The wrong treatment first, as standard
description: Six sessions of CBT for what is moral injury, or an SSRI for what is continuous traumatic stress about family still under threat. Not negligence - just the default pathway, applied to a case it was not designed for.
A psychiatric record can affect visa, asylum credibility, custody and citizenship in ways that vary by country and are rarely explained. Many people rationally decline treatment for this reason.
energy_note: Getting help, at the possible price of status.
notes: Interacts directly with the status and discretion issues in assets/text/iran.

aspect: SECONDARY - one bad experience ends help-seeking permanently
description: A dismissive first appointment produces a person who will not try again for fifteen years, and who tells their community not to bother either.
energy_note: One bad hour, a decade of nobody going.
